    Using evidence like a social scientist

    STATEMENT

    Small states can shape international rules despite having little hard power.

    EVIDENCE (with the source named)

    New Zealand signed the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons on the day it opened and ratified it on 31 July 2018, becoming the 14th state party; the treaty entered into force on 22 January 2021 and now has 75 states parties (ICAN, 2026).

    EXPLANATION (the bit most people skip)

    Early ratification mattered because the treaty needed 50 states to enter into force at all. A small state cannot force a great power to disarm, but it can help build the legal instrument that changes what counts as normal.

    QUALIFICATION (Excellence territory)

    No nuclear-armed state has joined, and warhead numbers are rising again. The treaty changes the law for those who accept it, not the arsenals of those who do not — so "influence" here means shifting the argument, not the weapons.
